contentBlocks.title: Declined — Your Guide to Appealing
contentBlocks.description: Your SASSA grant has been declined — you have the right to appeal. Discover the most common reasons for declines, your 90-day appeal window, and a step-by-step guide to filing a successful appeal with the Independent Tribunal.

contentBlocks.text: Declined — What It Means for Your SASSA Grant

Seeing 'Declined' on your SASSA status check can be frustrating, but it is not the end of the road. A declined status means SASSA's automated systems determined that you do not meet the eligibility criteria for the month being evaluated. Every month is assessed separately, and you have the legal right to appeal each declined month.
This status affects applicants whose SASSA grant applications did not meet the approval criteria after review.

contentBlocks.explanation: A 'Declined' status means SASSA's verification systems checked your application against their eligibility criteria and found a reason to reject your application for that specific month. SASSA checks multiple databases including Home Affairs, Department of Labour, SARS, NSFAS, and your bank account. A decline in one month does not mean you cannot qualify in future months.
whyItHappens: Alternative income source detected: bank deposits exceeded the R624 monthly threshold
UIF registration found: your ID is still linked to an active UIF record
NSFAS funding found: your ID is registered as an active NSFAS student
Means test failed: your income or assets exceed the legal limits
Bank verification failed: your bank details could not be confirmed
Identity verification failed: your ID details do not match Home Affairs records
Self exclusion: you declared you have other support
Referred for fraud investigation: your application was flagged for irregularities
Duplicate application detected: more than one application was submitted under your ID
contentBlocks.howLongItLasts: A declined status applies to a single monthly cycle. The following month is evaluated as a fresh application. However, if the underlying issue (e.g., UIF registration or bank deposits) persists, you may be declined again.
whatYouShouldDo: Check your decline notification for the specific reason code
If you believe the decline is incorrect, file an appeal within 90 days
For UIF-related declines: get a UI-19 termination letter from the Department of Labour
For NSFAS-related declines: request a cancellation letter from myNSFAS
For income source declines: prepare a sworn affidavit explaining bank deposits
For identity issues: visit Home Affairs to correct your details
Appeal each declined month separately on srd.dsd.gov.za

contentBlocks.title: You Have 90 Days to Appeal
contentBlocks.text: South African law gives you 90 days from the date of receiving your decline notification to file an appeal. Appeals are handled by the Independent Tribunal for Social Assistance Appeals (ITSAA), which is completely independent from SASSA. You do not need a lawyer to appeal.

faqs.question: Can I reapply instead of appealing?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can submit a new application at any time. However, if the reason for decline still exists (e.g., UIF registration), you will likely be declined again. Appeal or fix the underlying issue first.

faqs.question: Do I need to appeal every month?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because SASSA evaluates eligibility on a monthly basis, you must appeal for each individual month that shows 'Declined' status.

faqs.question: What if I missed the 90-day appeal window?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately, appeals cannot be accepted after 90 days. You must submit a completely new grant application.

faqs.question: Can I appeal in person at a SASSA office?
faqs.answer: Yes. For non-SRD grants, you can visit a SASSA office with your documents and request a manual appeal submission. For SRD, appeals are primarily handled online at srd.dsd.gov.za.

faqs.question: How long does the appeal process take?
faqs.answer: The tribunal typically takes 60 to 90 days to issue a ruling. If approved, SASSA must pay backdated amounts within 14 business days.
